Approach:
Create itr. Loop until its None and check: 
- if value equals itr's value, return False
- if value < node, assign new node if left is None else move left
- if value > node, assign new node if right is None else move right
Time & Space Complexity:
Average Case: O(log n)
Worst Case: O(n) [resembles LL 
when tree becomes unbalanced]
Edge Cases:
1. When BST has 0 node, root/itr will be None
Sol. Create new node and assign it as root. Return True

Approach:
Create itr. Loop until its None and check: 
- if value < node, then move left
- if value > node, then move right
- if value equals itr's value, return itr
Time & Space Complexity:
Average Case: O(log n)
Worst Case: O(n) (in an unbalanced tree)

Approach: Every Node points to either 0 or 2 nodes
Full tree + all leaf nodes should be present in last level
All nodes are as far left as possible without gaps

Each node has at most two children
Left subtree contains nodes with values less than parent's value
Right subtree contains nodes with values greater than parent's value
